body:
## Goal

Implement the next independent `gcs-engine` slice: a pure, immutable TypeScript
kernel that calculates GCS v5 trait current levels and adjusted point totals,
with semantic conformance proven against pinned GCS v5.44.0.

This issue is an implementation handoff. The approved design and TDD plan are
binding; do not redesign the public API or expand the product scope.

## Normative documents

Read these completely before implementation:

1. [Repository operating contract](https://github.com/CEHR2005/GCS-TS/blob/main/AGENTS.md)
2. [Engine-specific GCS invariants](https://github.com/CEHR2005/GCS-TS/blob/main/packages/gcs-engine/AGENTS.md)
3. [Approved trait cost calculation design](https://github.com/CEHR2005/GCS-TS/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-19-gcs-trait-cost-calculation-design.md)
4. [Task-by-task TDD implementation plan](https://github.com/CEHR2005/GCS-TS/blob/main/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-19-gcs-trait-cost-calculation.md)

If this issue conflicts with the approved design, stop and report the conflict.
If the plan is ambiguous but the design is clear, follow the design and record
the clarification in the Deviation Ledger.

## Exact baseline

Start from `main` commit
[`4f05a1e094013232bee2fcc484bd8ef64146f7a2`](https://github.com/CEHR2005/GCS-TS/commit/4f05a1e094013232bee2fcc484bd8ef64146f7a2).

Before edits, verify:

```sh
git rev-parse HEAD
git status --short --branch
```

The expected SHA is the value above and the worktree must be clean. If `main`
has advanced, stop and report the new SHA rather than silently rebasing the
approved plan onto a different baseline.

## Mandatory Superpowers preflight — fail closed

This task must use the official
`superpowers@openai-curated-remote` plugin. This is a hard prerequisite, not a
preference.

Before inspecting implementation details or changing repository files:

1. Confirm that the official plugin exposes `superpowers:using-superpowers`.
2. Invoke `superpowers:using-superpowers`.
3. Confirm that these workflows are callable:
   - `superpowers:using-git-worktrees`
   - `superpowers:subagent-driven-development`
   - `superpowers:test-driven-development`
   - `superpowers:systematic-debugging`
   - `superpowers:verification-before-completion`
   - `superpowers:requesting-code-review`
4. Confirm that Codex multi-agent support is enabled and subagent tools are
   callable. The effective configuration must include the equivalent of:

   ```toml
   [features]
   multi_agent = true
   ```

5. If the official plugin is absent, use the environment-supported plugin
   installation workflow to request exactly
   `superpowers@openai-curated-remote`, then reload/restart the solver session
   if the environment requires it.

Do not substitute a similarly named skill, a copied script, a hand-written
approximation, or an unpinned clone for the official plugin.

If installation, session reload, skill invocation, multi-agent enablement, or
subagent invocation is unavailable, stop immediately without implementation,
repository edits, commits, or generated files. Return the exact attempted
operation and error plus the human remediation needed. The prior Hive Mind
capability problem is tracked in
[link-assistant/hive-mind#2074](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/2074).

## Required execution workflow

After the preflight succeeds:

1. Invoke `superpowers:using-git-worktrees` and create an isolated feature
   worktree/branch from the exact baseline.
2. Invoke `superpowers:subagent-driven-development` and execute the approved
   plan task by task.
3. For every one of the eight plan tasks, use:
   - a fresh implementer subagent;
   - observed RED before production or bug-fix behavior;
   - the smallest GREEN implementation;
   - focused refactoring while tests remain green;
   - a fresh spec-compliance reviewer;
   - fixes for accepted spec findings through a new RED-GREEN cycle;
   - a fresh code-quality reviewer;
   - fixes for accepted quality findings through a new RED-GREEN cycle;
   - the task-specific verification commands and commit.
4. Use `superpowers:systematic-debugging` before proposing a fix for every
   unexpected test, build, oracle, Docker, or protocol failure.
5. After all tasks, use `superpowers:requesting-code-review` for a fresh
   whole-branch review.
6. Use `superpowers:verification-before-completion` and run the complete
   canonical gate after the final accepted change.

Do not use inline plan execution as a replacement for the mandated subagent
workflow. Independent read-only research may be parallelized, but code tasks
with shared files or ordering dependencies must follow the plan sequence.

## Canonical environment and source availability

The canonical gate is:

```sh
docker compose run --rm toolchain pnpm check
```

Use `sh -c`, not `sh -lc`, inside the toolchain container. Do not silently fall
back to host Node, pnpm, Go, or another environment.

Pinned sources of truth:

- `github.com/richardwilkes/gcs/v5` `v5.44.0`
- `github.com/richardwilkes/toolbox/v2` `v2.15.0`
- GCS Master Library fixtures from `v5.12.0`

The Go module pins and checksums are committed under
`tools/gcs-traits-oracle`. Docker image construction is the supported networked
dependency-resolution phase. Task 1 of the plan copies the resolved Go module
cache into the final toolchain and makes runtime Go tests use `GOPROXY=off`.

If pinned source inspection is needed before Task 1 is complete, use the
current canonical container and the committed module:

```sh
docker compose run --rm toolchain sh -c '
  go -C tools/gcs-traits-oracle mod download &&
  go -C tools/gcs-traits-oracle list -m -f "{{.Dir}}" \
    github.com/richardwilkes/gcs/v5
'
```

Record that runtime download as the known pre-Task-1 reproducibility gap; do
not treat it as the final state.

There is no required `/GCS`, `~/app/dragon-reaper/GCS`, or other host corpus.
Conformance must use the committed synthetic vectors, three committed fixtures,
and pinned modules. Tests must not fail merely because an uncommitted host path
is absent.

## Required implementation

Complete all eight tasks in the approved plan:

1. Copy the pinned Go module cache into the final Docker toolchain and prove all
   Go tests pass with `GOPROXY=off`.
2. Add the exact approved calculation types and stable boundary error model.
3. Add internal fixed-point fraction and permissive GCS `cost_adj` behavior.
4. Calculate leaf current levels and adjusted points in both modifier modes.
5. Add recursive containers, inherited modifiers, disabled propagation,
   alternative abilities, deep freezing, option validation, cycle/depth guards,
   package-root exports, and built-package smoke coverage.
6. Extend the existing Go traits oracle with strict `traits.calculate`; do not
   create a fourth Go module or call `Entity.Recalculate`.
7. Add strict TypeScript runner/protocol tests and differential conformance for
   deterministic vectors plus Wang Laowu, Dragon, and Lich in both modes.
8. Update package/root documentation and precise third-party provenance.

The production data flow remains:

```text
GcsDocumentV5
  -> projectGcsTraitsV5()
  -> calculateGcsTraitPointsV5()
  -> readonly calculation result tree
```

Production remains TypeScript-only and has zero runtime dependencies. All
translated calculation behavior stays inside the MPL-2.0 `packages/gcs-engine`
boundary.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The exact approved public API is exported from the built package, with no
      additional public contract invented by the implementation.
- [ ] `calculateGcsTraitPointsV5` consumes only the typed projection and never
      mutates or aliases its input.
- [ ] Result order, TIDs, discriminants, recursive structure, and absent versus
      empty collections are retained in deeply frozen output.
- [ ] Missing/non-boolean options, cycles, and depth overflow produce the exact
      approved code and JSON-pointer path.
- [ ] Leaf, CR/frequency, modifier, leveled modifier, rounding, disabled,
      inheritance, regular-container, and alternative-ability semantics match
      pinned GCS nil-entity behavior.
- [ ] Both additive and multiplicative modifier modes are covered.
- [ ] Permissive decimal, fractional, malformed, ASCII `x`, and Unicode `×`
      `cost_adj` cases are differential- or unit-tested as specified.
- [ ] Entity-derived level bonuses remain demonstrably zero; the oracle does
      not call `NewEntity` or `Recalculate`.
- [ ] Synthetic vectors and all three committed fixtures pass conformance in
      both modes.
- [ ] Existing parse, serialize, primitive, and trait projection behavior stays
      green.
- [ ] `packages/gcs-engine` has no runtime dependency and production has no Go
      requirement.
- [ ] All Go tests pass with `GOPROXY=off` after the Docker build.
- [ ] `docker compose run --rm toolchain pnpm check` passes after the final
      whole-branch review.
- [ ] Each plan task has its implementer commit plus completed fresh spec and
      quality review gates.
- [ ] The complete diff contains no secrets, host-specific paths, generated
      caches, unrelated refactors, or unapproved `AGENTS.md` edits.

## Out of scope

- Full `Entity.Recalculate`, features, entity trait bonuses, and public
  calculation traces.
- Reading sheet settings from generic document JSON or writing `calc`.
- Trait/modifier create, update, delete, duplicate, toggle, move, or write-back.
- Skills, spells, equipment, weapons, attributes, or encumbrance calculation.
- Search, DnD, folders, context menus, Next.js, shadcn/ui, Prisma, PostgreSQL,
  authentication, or deployment.
- GCS versions other than v5.
- Production Go, a new production dependency, a fourth oracle module, or a
  canonical dependency on an uncommitted host corpus.
- Refactoring unrelated foundation, primitive, or projection code.

## Stop conditions

Stop cleanly and report evidence instead of applying a workaround if:

- the mandatory official Superpowers or multi-agent preflight fails;
- the exact baseline cannot be obtained cleanly;
- the approved design requires a material public API/architecture change;
- pinned GCS behavior cannot be established from the committed module pins;
- Docker cannot provide the canonical environment;
- a dependency, security, licensing, or compatibility problem requires a
  material decision;
- an acceptance criterion would need to be weakened or skipped.

Never use `--force`, `--legacy-peer-deps`, blanket ignores, disabled tests,
unsafe broad casts, copied dependency code, host-specific hardcoding, or a
silent environment fallback.

## Delivery

After all acceptance criteria and reviews pass:

1. Review the complete diff and Deviation Ledger.
2. Ensure all task commits are on one feature branch based on the exact
   baseline.
3. Push that feature branch and open a pull request targeting `main`.
4. Do not merge the pull request.
5. In the PR and final solver report, include:
   - outcome and changed behavior;
   - commit list;
   - exact verification commands and observed counts/results;
   - task-level and whole-branch review results;
   - decisions and assumptions;
   - complete Deviation Ledger;
   - remaining risks/follow-ups;
   - an exact `AGENTS.md candidate`, or `No update recommended`.

Do not claim a check passed if it was not run. Do not claim completion while a
material acceptance criterion remains unverified. State `No silent workaround
was used` only if it is factually true.
title: Implement GCS v5 trait cost calculation kernel
